project.name: ORISO-Keycloak
project.description: Keycloak realm and deployment configuration for ORISO identity, authentication, authorization, token issuance, and IAM integration.

nodes.name: app-custom scope
nodes.summary: The app-custom client scope maps username, tenantId, and userId user attributes into access, ID, and userinfo tokens.

nodes.name: Backend token validation
nodes.summary: Backend services validate JWTs through the realm issuer URI and JWK set URI, then read roles and tenant/user claims.

nodes.name: Environment drift
nodes.summary: Docs reference direct IPs, Nginx /auth proxy paths, auth.oriso.site ingress, current realm sslRequired=external, and scripts that set sslRequired=NONE.

nodes.name: Frontend OIDC login
nodes.summary: Frontend/admin clients authenticate through the public app client using browser-based OIDC authorization code flow.

nodes.name: HTTP access mode
nodes.summary: Docs and scripts intentionally disable SSL requirement for internal HTTP access while relying on proxy/TLS termination.

nodes.name: kcadm admin automation
nodes.summary: configure-http-access.sh and backup/realm-backup.sh use kcadm inside the running Keycloak pod to change realm settings and export configuration.

nodes.name: Keycloak as central IAM
nodes.summary: ORISO-Keycloak is the identity provider for ORISO services, issuing OIDC tokens and centralizing user role management.

nodes.name: No groups configured
nodes.summary: realm.json exports an empty groups array; group-based authorization is not currently modeled in this repository.

nodes.name: No external identity providers
nodes.summary: identityProviders is empty; SSO is internal to Keycloak, with no Google/Azure/SAML/social broker configured in this realm export.

nodes.name: online-beratung realm
nodes.summary: The online-beratung realm is the tenant for ORISO identity configuration in realm.json.

nodes.name: Realm roles authorization
nodes.summary: ORISO authorization is role-driven through realm_access.roles, including tenant-admin, agency-admin, consultant, user, and technical roles.

nodes.name: Hardcoded admin credentials
nodes.summary: keycloak-deployment.yaml and scripts use admin/admin directly instead of Kubernetes Secrets.

nodes.name: Long token lifetimes
nodes.summary: Access tokens last 18000 seconds and implicit-flow access token lifespan is 54000 seconds, increasing exposure if tokens leak.

nodes.name: start-dev runtime risk
nodes.summary: The Deployment runs Keycloak with start-dev, no external database configuration, no probes, no resource limits, and hostNetwork enabled.

nodes.name: Weak realm security defaults
nodes.summary: Brute force protection, password policy, email verification, event logging, and admin event logging are disabled or absent.

nodes.name: Wide redirect and CORS risk
nodes.summary: The app client allows wildcard redirect URI and web origin entries, plus localhost and public IP HTTP origins.

nodes.name: Tenant isolation by tenantId claim
nodes.summary: Tenant isolation is represented by a user attribute mapped into the tenantId token claim; services enforce tenant boundaries from the token, not Keycloak groups.

tour.title: Start with the realm export
tour.description: realm.json is the source of truth in this repository. It defines online-beratung, the app client, realm roles, token scopes, required actions, and authentication flows.

tour.title: Understand the app client
tour.description: The app client is the ORISO frontend/admin OIDC client. It enables standard authorization flow and direct access grants, includes app-custom and roles scopes, and currently uses broad redirect/web-origin settings.

tour.title: Trace token claims
tour.description: app-custom maps username, tenantId, and userId user attributes into access, ID, and userinfo tokens. Backend services rely on tenantId and realm roles for tenant-aware authorization.

tour.title: Review auth flows
tour.description: The realm uses the built-in browser flow for login and direct grant for password token requests. OTP is conditional when the user has configured it.

tour.title: Review runtime configuration
tour.description: Kubernetes manifests run Keycloak 20.0.5 with start-dev, hostNetwork, HTTP enabled, and auth.oriso.site ingress. These are the main DevOps-owned files.

tour.title: Review operations scripts
tour.description: configure-http-access.sh changes sslRequired after deployment, while backup/realm-backup.sh exports the realm back into this repository. Both assume admin credentials and the caritas namespace.

tour.title: Review the risk map
tour.description: The highest priority production issues are hardcoded admin credentials, start-dev runtime, wildcard app redirects/web origins, weak realm defaults, long token lifetimes, and environment drift between docs, scripts, and realm export.
